evidence: Anterior cruciate ligament: The distal bony avulsion with laxity of the ACL, showing some internal high T2 signal changes compatible with additional low-grade partial ligamentous tear.

Medial collateral ligament: Complete tear of the superficial portion at the mid to distal third. Moderate grade partial tear of the deep meniscal femoral and meniscal tibial components with partial meniscocapsular separation of the medial meniscal body.

Medial meniscus: Mild nonspecific signal changes of the meniscal body, with evidence of small horizontal oblique tear extending to the femoral surface. No other significant tear. Bony avulsion of the posterior horn root insertion as detailed above.

Lateral meniscus: Mild nonspecific signal changes at the anterior horn compatible with low-grade tearing. Evidence of small Wrisberg rip-type longitudinal tear of the periphery of the posterior horn. Complete tear of the inferior meniscal popliteal fascicle compatible with posterior lateral corner injury. There is a bony avulsion of the anterior horn and posterior horn root insertion sites.

Fractures:
Known mildly comminuted undisplaced avulsion fracture of the tibial tuberosity involving the distal ACL insertion, anteriorly the anterior horn root insertion of the lateral meniscus, as well as posteriorly the tibial insertion of both the posterior horn of medial and lateral menisci. There is associated bone marrow edema associated with these fractures.
